  error_rate: 0.08 # "errors" only

  # Inputs for call_genotype() function

  HT_min_frequence: 0.20 # minor allele must be larger or equal to call HT

  # Inputs for strand check filter or flag
  strand_flag_prob: 0.01 # strand check, a direction needs at least 8 reads before its flagged

  prior_het_share: 0.15 # only for prior_type = "het_share": prior probability of a heterozygote (the two homozygotes share the rest)
  prior_population: "FreqWOLF_all" # only used when prior_type == "hwe": FreqWOLF_all, FreqWOLF_EastEurope, FreqWOLF_IT, FreqWOLF_IB, FreqDOG
  prior_floor: 0.001 # floors for allele frequency
  ancestry_prior_shape: 1 # only for prior_type = "ancestry": Beta(shape, shape) prior on wolf ancestry, 1 = uniform, 0.5 = leans to pure animals
  phi_hom_structure: "shared" # homozygote overdispersion: "shared" (one value), "locus", "sample" or "locus_sample"
  
  # Downsampling and genotype confidence calibration
  read_depths_to_test: [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 75]
  draws_per_depth: 300 # random draws per pair and read depth
  minimum_reads_for_truth_pair: 75 # a pair needs at least this many reads, so even the deepest draws are real subsamples
  bootstrap_rounds: 1000 # bootstrap datasets for the confidence bands

## Downsampling and genotype confidence calibration
This is the validation step of the Bayes model. Idea behind it is to check how sure the genotyper is about every calls and if it only had a certain amount of reads available would the end results, the final genotype be the same? At full depth with many reads and data to work with, practically both genotyper are correct which gives good results but the information about the miscall and samples with low depth is more important. Idea is to check how the model handles lowers depth data for pairs where the final answer is known and correct, lower depth samples are created artificially from higher depth data which is called downsampling. It chooses sample with over 75 reads, it produces sub samples from 3, 4, 5, 6, 10 ... 75 reads and repeats it 100 per subsample. I test 12 depths, 100 times, for 740 pairs, from those calls error rate can be computed and the GQ confidence can be tested for the model, is a GQ 20 call relly GQ 20?

Pairs used for the downsampling:  with more than 75 reads, have a reference and its final call matches the reference (667 HM and 82 HT).
Downsampling is done for both naive caller and bayes model with imported info about parameters from previous stan call (posterior, error rate, prior,...). GQ results are then s grouped into 0-5, 5- 10, ..., 50+ bins.
Calibration per GQ bin, what Stan claimed (max posterior) against what was the correct result (bins with zero wrongs calls get Wilson upper  bound, error cant be zero)
For every depth error rate is calculated, split into HT and HM.

Calibration statistics are calculated for the stan calls: Brier score, Brier skill score, ECE, Spiegelhalter Z (for all, and HM HT separately). Calibration is needed to check how over or under confident the model is or HT and HM calls, it checks if calls with 1 % error rate are actually wrong 1 % of the time. For example: If HM calls have 2.7 % error rate and were wrong 0.8 % they are too cautious, and if my HT calls have error rate of about  5.4 % and were wrong 10 % of the time they are too confident. Brier score is the average of squared (claimed probability - 0 or 1), where minus 1 when right and -0 when wrong. Lower score is better. Because the naive caller is always 100 % sure its Brier score is just the error rate. Brier skill score, compares Brier score with a simple forecaster which give every call the same overall accuracy. If its above 0 it means  Stans individual probabilities add information, below 0 means they are worse than just one flat number. ECE is the expected calibration error, its the average gaps between the observed and claimed  error across all GQ bins, weighted by the number of calls in the bin (0 is perfect). Spiegelhalter Z is a significance tedt of calibration, at around 0 it means it's calibrated, above +2 over confident, below -2 too cautious,

Bootstraping, it gives uncertantiy bands for results. Treatinf every downsampled call as independent is incorrect because all the subsampled read cluster come from the same locus sample pair. If the original pair for lets say HT inherits some unnusal split of 35:65, all the subsamples will as well. There are really 749 independent pairs. treating every call as indepdent would make the boostrapped bands too narrow. It draws with replacememnt from 749 pairs HM and HT separately, recomputes error rates and statisctis. 

Plot for GQ threshold trade off, if i use it as a filter, how many call are kept and how many of the errors can i get rid of.

```{r Downsampling_Calibration_Compute}

dir.create(downsampling_output_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Reference genotypes and settings
reference_genotypes_file <- file.path("Data/Supporting_data/Reference_genotypes", paste0("genotypes_", dataset_name, ".tsv"))
read_depths_to_test <- unlist(read_depths_to_test) # the YAML list becomes a plain number vector
gq_bin_edges <- c(seq(0, 30, by = 2.5), 35, 40, 50, Inf) 
gq_thresholds_to_test <- 1:40 # GQ thresholds for the trade-off plot
stopifnot("the deepest read depth to test must not be larger than minimum_reads_for_truth_pair" = max(read_depths_to_test) <= minimum_reads_for_truth_pair)

### Helper functions
# Makes sure the alleles are always in the same alpabetical order (reference panel was not created inside the script, so it might have different labels)
sort_alleles_in_genotype <- function(genotype) ifelse(is.na(genotype), NA_character_,
                                                      paste0(pmin(substr(genotype, 1, 1), substr(genotype, 2, 2)),
                                                             pmax(substr(genotype, 1, 1), substr(genotype, 2, 2))))

# Stans genotype function, it computes three genotype probabilities the same way as .stan file does with k allele 1 reads out of d possible reads. It uses the values the fitted model learned from for that specific locus sample pair. This is the part of the analysis which enables downsampling without running stan again which would take a lot longer.
stan_genotype_posterior <- function(k, d, error_rate, het_fraction, phi_het, phi_hom, genotype_prior) {
  log_beta_binomial <- function(k, d, a, b) lchoose(d, k) + lbeta(k + a, d - k + b) - lbeta(a, b)
  het_allele1_share <- het_fraction * (1 - error_rate) + (1 - het_fraction) * error_rate # read errors inside HT
  log_likelihoods <- cbind(log_beta_binomial(k, d, (1 - error_rate) * phi_hom, error_rate * phi_hom), # HM1
                           log_beta_binomial(k, d, error_rate * phi_hom, (1 - error_rate) * phi_hom), # HM2
                           log_beta_binomial(k, d, het_allele1_share * phi_het, (1 - het_allele1_share) * phi_het)) #HT
  log_prior_times_likelihood <- log(genotype_prior) + log_likelihoods # prior * likelihood in log (+)
  scaled_values <- exp(log_prior_times_likelihood - apply(log_prior_times_likelihood, 1, max)) # subtract the max first, to avoid really small values (end results is the same because the exp(A - n) = exp(A) * exp-(n), the exp(-n) cancels in the division)
  scaled_values / rowSums(scaled_values) # divided by their sum = posterior (with a flat prior this is the normalised likelihood)
}
### Step 1: fitted model values and the reference set

# Table of every learned parameter for each pair for the downsampling, error rates, overdispersion values, prior, .... 
fitted_pair_error_rates <- data.frame(
  barcode = counts_hier$barcode,
  locus = counts_hier$locus,
  error_rate_pair = colMeans(extract(fit_hier, "error_rate")$error_rate), # posterior mean per pair
  phi_het_pair = colMeans(draws_hier$phi_het_sample)[match(counts_hier$barcode, samples_hier)], 
  phi_hom_pair = colMeans(draws_hier$phi_hom_pair), # homozygote overdispersion of every pair (shared, per locus and/or per sample)
  prior_hom1 = pair_prior_hier[, "prior_hom1"],
  prior_hom2 = pair_prior_hier[, "prior_hom2"],
  prior_het = pair_prior_hier[, "prior_het"])

# Ancestry prior in downsampling without reusing evidence. Each pairs prior comes from wolf ancestry of its sample estimated from the other loci only. A downsampled pairs is never scored based on a prior built with the full depth of reads, so the evidence of the locus is not reused when doing the downsampling. Ancestry posterior is evaluated on a grid from the called genotypes and fixed wolf or dog allele frequencies  (hybrid-index likelihood, Buerkle 2005).
if (prior_type == "ancestry") {
  ancestry_grid <- seq(0.0005, 0.9995, by = 0.001) # every wolf ancestry value that is tried
  pair_genotype_class <- max.col(post_hier, ties.method = "first") # full-depth call of every pair: 1 = hom1, 2 = hom2, 3 = het
  grid_allele1_p <- outer(ancestry_grid, stan_data_hier$p_wolf[stan_data_hier$locus_id]) +
    outer(1 - ancestry_grid, stan_data_hier$p_dog[stan_data_hier$locus_id]) # allele1 frequency for every ancestry value (rows) and pair (columns)
  called_class <- matrix(pair_genotype_class, nrow = length(ancestry_grid), ncol = length(pair_genotype_class), byrow = TRUE)
  log_called_genotype <- log(ifelse(called_class == 1, grid_allele1_p^2,
                                    ifelse(called_class == 2, (1 - grid_allele1_p)^2, 2 * grid_allele1_p * (1 - grid_allele1_p)))) # how likely each pair's call is under each ancestry value
  log_sample_total <- t(rowsum(t(log_called_genotype), stan_data_hier$sample_id)) # summed over all loci of each sample
  log_without_own_locus <- log_sample_total[, stan_data_hier$sample_id] - log_called_genotype +
    dbeta(ancestry_grid, ancestry_prior_shape, ancestry_prior_shape, log = TRUE) # the pair's own locus taken out, Beta prior added
  ancestry_weights <- exp(sweep(log_without_own_locus, 2, apply(log_without_own_locus, 2, max))) # max subtracted first to avoid tiny numbers
  ancestry_weights <- sweep(ancestry_weights, 2, colSums(ancestry_weights), "/") # weights of every pair sum to 1
  fitted_pair_error_rates$prior_hom1 <- colSums(ancestry_weights * grid_allele1_p^2)
  fitted_pair_error_rates$prior_hom2 <- colSums(ancestry_weights * (1 - grid_allele1_p)^2)
  fitted_pair_error_rates$prior_het <- colSums(ancestry_weights * 2 * grid_allele1_p * (1 - grid_allele1_p))
}

# Importing reference genotypes
reference_genotypes <- read_tsv(reference_genotypes_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(barcode = sample_id, locus, reference = genotype)

# Truth pairs which match every criteria for the downsampling, they have a reference, are correct and have enough reads 
truth_pairs <- combined_genotypes_hier %>%
  filter(status == "called", depth >= minimum_reads_for_truth_pair) %>%
  inner_join(reference_genotypes, by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(reference)) %>%
  mutate(reference_sorted = sort_alleles_in_genotype(reference)) %>%
  filter(reference_sorted == sort_alleles_in_genotype(genotype_naive)) %>%
  select(barcode, locus, reference_sorted) %>%
  left_join(panel[, c("locus", "allele1", "allele2")], by = "locus") %>%
  left_join(fitted_pair_error_rates, by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
  left_join(locus_params_hier[, c("locus", "het_fraction")], by = "locus") %>%
  mutate(pair_id = paste(barcode, locus, sep = "|"),
         true_class = ifelse(substr(reference_sorted, 1, 1) == substr(reference_sorted, 2, 2), "True homozygotes", "True heterozygotes"))

cat(sprintf("Truth set: %d pairs (%d homozygous, %d heterozygous) with >= %d reads and a full-depth call matching the reference | Stan prior: %s\n",
            nrow(truth_pairs), sum(truth_pairs$true_class == "True homozygotes"),
            sum(truth_pairs$true_class == "True heterozygotes"), minimum_reads_for_truth_pair, prior_label_hier))

# All the usable reads from the pipeline and returns small table for every pair
reads_by_truth_pair <- reads_hier %>%
  filter(!is.na(called_allele)) %>%
  mutate(pair_id = paste(barcode, locus, sep = "|")) %>%
  filter(pair_id %in% truth_pairs$pair_id) %>%
  select(pair_id, called_allele, direction) %>%
  split(~ pair_id)

### Step 2: Draw reads and naive calls

# Downsampling function
downsample_and_call_one_pair <- function(pair_id) {
  pair_reads <- reads_by_truth_pair[[pair_id]] 
  allele1_of_pair <- truth_pairs$allele1[match(pair_id, truth_pairs$pair_id)]
  depth_of_each_draw <- rep(read_depths_to_test, each = draws_per_depth) # draws needed
  allele1_reads_in_draw <- integer(length(depth_of_each_draw)) # k
  naive_genotype <- character(length(depth_of_each_draw)) # naive call, with the pipeline's strand setting
  for (i in seq_along(depth_of_each_draw)) {
    kept_reads <- sample.int(nrow(pair_reads), depth_of_each_draw[i]) # picks random reads without replacement
    kept_alleles <- pair_reads$called_allele[kept_reads]
    allele1_reads_in_draw[i] <- sum(kept_alleles == allele1_of_pair)
    naive_genotype[i] <- unname(call_genotype(kept_alleles, pair_reads$direction[kept_reads],
                                              minimum_required_depth = minimum_required_depth, HT_min_frequence = HT_min_frequence,
                                              strand_flag_prob = strand_flag_prob, expected_minor_fraction = expected_minor_fraction,
                                              strand_downgrade = strand_downgrade)["genotype"])
  }
  data.frame(pair_id = pair_id, depth = depth_of_each_draw, k = allele1_reads_in_draw, genotype_naive = naive_genotype)
}

# Random number generator which works in parallel
default_random_generator <- RNGkind()[1]
RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG") # switch to reproducible random numbers across mclapply workers, with no overlap
set.seed(1) # same for every run
t0 <- Sys.time()

# Running the downsampling
downsampled_list <- mclapply(truth_pairs$pair_id, downsample_and_call_one_pair, mc.cores = n_cores)
RNGkind(default_random_generator) # back to the session's default generator
failed_pairs <- vapply(downsampled_list, function(result) is.null(result) || inherits(result, "try-error"), logical(1)) # mclapply returns errors (or NULL for a killed worker) instead of stopping # Checks for error, mclapply doesnt stop just produces error object
first_failed <- which(failed_pairs)[1]
if (any(failed_pairs)) stop(sprintf("downsampling failed for %d of %d pairs. First error (%s): %s",
                                    sum(failed_pairs), length(failed_pairs), truth_pairs$pair_id[first_failed],
                                    if (is.null(downsampled_list[[first_failed]])) "no result, worker was killed (often out of memory)" else downsampled_list[[first_failed]]))
# Combined table
downsampled_draws <- bind_rows(downsampled_list)
log_time(sprintf("downsampling: %d pairs x %d depths x %d draws", nrow(truth_pairs), length(read_depths_to_test), draws_per_depth), t0)

### Step 3: Stan downsampling and scoring

#Joins the dowssampling draws table with the data table of all the stans genotype probabilites
downsampled_draws_with_parameters <- downsampled_draws %>%
  left_join(select(truth_pairs, -barcode, -locus), by = "pair_id")

stan_posteriors <- stan_genotype_posterior(downsampled_draws_with_parameters$k, downsampled_draws_with_parameters$depth,
                                           downsampled_draws_with_parameters$error_rate_pair, downsampled_draws_with_parameters$het_fraction,
                                           downsampled_draws_with_parameters$phi_het_pair, downsampled_draws_with_parameters$phi_hom_pair,
                                           genotype_prior = as.matrix(downsampled_draws_with_parameters[, c("prior_hom1", "prior_hom2", "prior_het")]))
stan_best_genotype <- max.col(stan_posteriors, ties.method = "first") # 1 = HM1, 2 = HM2, 3 = HT

# Scored calls and genotypes with all the statistics for error by depth, calibration, trade-off plots
downsampled_calls_scored <- downsampled_draws_with_parameters %>%
  mutate(genotype_stan = ifelse(stan_best_genotype == 1, paste0(allele1, allele1),
                          ifelse(stan_best_genotype == 2, paste0(allele2, allele2), paste0(pmin(allele1, allele2), pmax(allele1, allele2)))),
         max_posterior_stan = pmax(stan_posteriors[, 1], stan_posteriors[, 2], stan_posteriors[, 3]),
         GQ_stan = pmin(99, -10 * log10(pmax(1 - max_posterior_stan, 1e-10))),
         gq_bin = cut(GQ_stan, gq_bin_edges, right = FALSE),
         naive_no_call = is.na(genotype_naive),
         naive_wrong = !naive_no_call & sort_alleles_in_genotype(genotype_naive) != reference_sorted,
         stan_wrong = genotype_stan != reference_sorted,
         called_class = ifelse(substr(genotype_stan, 1, 1) == substr(genotype_stan, 2, 2), "Homozygous calls", "Heterozygous calls"))

### Step 5: Per pair bootstrap

# Prep for the bootstrap: every matrix has one row per truth pair (in truth_pairs order) and one column per depth or GQ bin
is_homozygous_pair <- truth_pairs$true_class == "True homozygotes"
homozygous_rows <- which(is_homozygous_pair)
heterozygous_rows <- which(!is_homozygous_pair)
depth_groups <- list(`All pairs` = rep(TRUE, nrow(truth_pairs)),
                     `True homozygotes` = is_homozygous_pair,
                     `True heterozygotes` = !is_homozygous_pair)
calibration_groups <- c("All calls", "Homozygous calls", "Heterozygous calls")

# Per pair counts for each depth: tapply sums every pair x depth cell, empty cells get 0
pair_factor <- factor(downsampled_calls_scored$pair_id, levels = truth_pairs$pair_id)
pair_and_depth <- list(pair_factor, factor(downsampled_calls_scored$depth, levels = read_depths_to_test))
naive_calls_by_depth <- tapply(!downsampled_calls_scored$naive_no_call, pair_and_depth, sum, default = 0)
naive_wrong_by_depth <- tapply(downsampled_calls_scored$naive_wrong, pair_and_depth, sum, default = 0)
stan_wrong_by_depth <- tapply(downsampled_calls_scored$stan_wrong, pair_and_depth, sum, default = 0)

# Per pair counts for each GQ bin, separately for all, homozygous and heterozygous calls
calibration_inputs <- sapply(calibration_groups, function(group_name) {
  in_group <- group_name == "All calls" | downsampled_calls_scored$called_class == group_name
  group_calls <- downsampled_calls_scored[in_group, ]
  pair_and_bin <- list(pair_factor[in_group], group_calls$gq_bin)
  list(calls = tapply(group_calls$stan_wrong, pair_and_bin, length, default = 0),
       wrong = tapply(group_calls$stan_wrong, pair_and_bin, sum, default = 0),
       claimed = tapply(1 - group_calls$max_posterior_stan, pair_and_bin, sum, default = 0),
       brier_sum = tapply((group_calls$max_posterior_stan - !group_calls$stan_wrong)^2, pair_factor[in_group], sum, default = 0))
}, simplify = FALSE)

gq_bin_names <- levels(downsampled_calls_scored$gq_bin)

# Bootstraping
set.seed(2)
t0 <- Sys.time()
bootstrap_depth_rounds <- vector("list", bootstrap_rounds)
bootstrap_calibration_rounds <- vector("list", bootstrap_rounds)
bootstrap_statistics_rounds <- vector("list", bootstrap_rounds)
for (round_number in seq_len(bootstrap_rounds)) {
  pair_weights <- tabulate(c(homozygous_rows[sample.int(length(homozygous_rows), replace = TRUE)],
                             heterozygous_rows[sample.int(length(heterozygous_rows), replace = TRUE)]),
                           nbins = nrow(truth_pairs)) # how often each pair is drawn this round, homozygous and heterozygous drawn separately

  bootstrap_depth_rounds[[round_number]] <- bind_rows(lapply(names(depth_groups), function(group_name) {
    weights_in_group <- pair_weights * depth_groups[[group_name]]
    naive_rate <- as.vector(weights_in_group %*% naive_wrong_by_depth) / as.vector(weights_in_group %*% naive_calls_by_depth)
    stan_rate <- as.vector(weights_in_group %*% stan_wrong_by_depth) / (sum(weights_in_group) * draws_per_depth)
    data.frame(round = round_number, group = group_name, depth = read_depths_to_test,
               naive = naive_rate, stan = stan_rate, difference = naive_rate - stan_rate)
  }))

  bootstrap_calibration_rounds[[round_number]] <- bind_rows(lapply(calibration_groups, function(group_name) {
    observed <- as.vector(pair_weights %*% calibration_inputs[[group_name]]$wrong) /
                as.vector(pair_weights %*% calibration_inputs[[group_name]]$calls)
    data.frame(round = round_number, group = group_name, gq_bin = gq_bin_names, observed_error = observed)
  }))

  bootstrap_statistics_rounds[[round_number]] <- bind_rows(lapply(calibration_groups, function(group_name) {
    inputs <- calibration_inputs[[group_name]]
    calls_drawn <- sum(pair_weights %*% inputs$calls)
    data.frame(round = round_number, group = group_name,
               brier = sum(pair_weights * inputs$brier_sum) / calls_drawn,
               ece = sum(abs(pair_weights %*% (inputs$wrong - inputs$claimed))) / calls_drawn) # ECE = |wrong - claimed| errors over all calls
  }))
}

# Combining all the result tables
bootstrap_depth_results <- bind_rows(bootstrap_depth_rounds)
bootstrap_calibration_results <- bind_rows(bootstrap_calibration_rounds)
bootstrap_statistics_results <- bind_rows(bootstrap_statistics_rounds)
log_time(sprintf("pair bootstrap: %d rounds", bootstrap_rounds), t0)

### Step 4: error rate and read depth

# Data prep and finals tables for the plots, this table stack the results twice once labelled as all pairs once by the true class (for groups by step)
calls_by_true_class <- bind_rows(mutate(downsampled_calls_scored, group = "All pairs"),
                                 mutate(downsampled_calls_scored, group = true_class))

# results per group and depth
error_by_depth_estimates <- calls_by_true_class %>%
  group_by(group, depth) %>%
  summarise(Naive = sum(naive_wrong) / sum(!naive_no_call),
            `Hierarchical Stan` = mean(stan_wrong),
            naive_no_calls = sum(naive_no_call),
            n_calls = n(), n_pairs = n_distinct(pair_id), .groups = "drop")

# Boostraping bands
depth_bands <- bootstrap_depth_results %>%
  group_by(group, depth) %>%
  summarise(naive_low = quantile(naive, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), naive_high = quantile(naive, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
            stan_low = quantile(stan, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), stan_high = quantile(stan, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
            difference_low = quantile(difference, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), difference_high = quantile(difference, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

error_by_depth_table <- error_by_depth_estimates %>%
  mutate(difference = Naive - `Hierarchical Stan`) %>%
  left_join(depth_bands, by = c("group", "depth")) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = names(depth_groups)))
kable(error_by_depth_table %>%
        select(group, depth, Naive, `Hierarchical Stan`, difference, difference_low, difference_high) %>%
        mutate(across(-c(group, depth), ~ round(100 * .x, 3))),
      col.names = c("Group", "Reads", "Naive error (%)", "Stan error (%)", "Difference (pp)", "Band low", "Band high"))

### Step 5: statistics for calibration plots

# Data prep and finals tables for calibration plot, this table stack the results twice once labelled as all pairs once by the called class (for groupt by step)
calls_by_called_class <- bind_rows(mutate(downsampled_calls_scored, group = "All calls"),
                                   mutate(downsampled_calls_scored, group = called_class))

calibration_counts <- calls_by_called_class %>%
  group_by(group, gq_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), n_pairs = n_distinct(pair_id), n_wrong = sum(stan_wrong),
            claimed_error = mean(1 - max_posterior_stan), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(gq_bin = as.character(gq_bin))



calibration_statistics_estimates <- calls_by_called_class %>%
  mutate(correct = as.numeric(!stan_wrong), claimed_correct = max_posterior_stan, # 1 and 0 for right or wrong, max posteriors and prep for spiegelhalter Ztest
         spiegelhalter_term = (correct - claimed_correct) * (1 - 2 * claimed_correct)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(n_calls = n(),
            accuracy = mean(correct),
            mean_claimed_error = mean(1 - claimed_correct),
            observed_error = 1 - mean(correct),
            brier = mean((claimed_correct - correct)^2), # the lower the better
            reference_brier = mean(correct) * (1 - mean(correct)), # brier where every call has the same overall accuracy
            spiegelhalter_z_cluster = { #if Z is more than +2 its overconfident, if its lower than -2 it too cautious
              per_pair_terms <- tapply(spiegelhalter_term, pair_id, sum) 
              sum(per_pair_terms) / sqrt(sum(per_pair_terms^2))
            },
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(brier_skill_score = 1 - brier / reference_brier)

ece_estimates <- calibration_counts %>%
  summarise(ece = sum(abs(n_wrong - n * claimed_error)) / sum(n), .by = group) # |observed - claimed| errors over all calls divided by all calls

# Bands for the 1000 bootstraped rounds
statistics_bands <- bootstrap_statistics_results %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(brier_low = quantile(brier, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), brier_high = quantile(brier, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
            ece_low = quantile(ece, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), ece_high = quantile(ece, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Naive caller is always "100 %" certain so its Brier score is its error rate (over its calls, no-calls excluded)
naive_brier_equivalent <- sum(downsampled_calls_scored$naive_wrong) / sum(!downsampled_calls_scored$naive_no_call) 

# Joins all the estimates
calibration_statistics_table <- calibration_statistics_estimates %>%
  left_join(ece_estimates, by = "group") %>%
  left_join(statistics_bands, by = "group") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = calibration_groups),
         prior = prior_label_hier) %>%
  arrange(group)
kable(calibration_statistics_table %>%
        transmute(group, n_calls,
                  observed_error_pct = round(100 * observed_error, 2), mean_claimed_error_pct = round(100 * mean_claimed_error, 2),
                  brier = signif(brier, 3), brier_95 = sprintf("%.4f-%.4f", brier_low, brier_high),
                  brier_skill_score = round(brier_skill_score, 3),
                  ece_pct = round(100 * ece, 2), ece_95 = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", 100 * ece_low, 100 * ece_high),
                  spiegelhalter_z_cluster = round(spiegelhalter_z_cluster, 2)),
      col.names = c("Calls", "n", "Observed error (%)", "Claimed error (%)", "Brier", "Brier 95 %", "Brier skill", "ECE (%)", "ECE 95 %", "Spiegelhalter Z"),
      format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

cat(sprintf("Naive caller (claims certainty) Brier-equivalent = its error rate: %.4f | hierarchical Stan Brier (all calls, %s): %.4f\n",
            naive_brier_equivalent, prior_label_hier, calibration_statistics_table$brier[calibration_statistics_table$group == "All calls"]))

### Step 6: Calibration table per GQ bin

# 95 % bands for each group and GQ bin
calibration_bands <- bootstrap_calibration_results %>%
  group_by(group, gq_bin) %>%
  summarise(boot_error_low = quantile(observed_error, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
            boot_error_high = quantile(observed_error, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Data prep for calibration plot
calibration_table <- calibration_counts %>%
  left_join(calibration_bands, by = c("group", "gq_bin")) %>%
  mutate(
    observed_error = n_wrong / n,
    zero_error_upper = ifelse(n_wrong == 0, 1.96^2 / (n + 1.96^2), NA), # 95 % Wilson upper bound for zero wrongs calls cases
    claimed_Q = pmin(60, -10 * log10(pmax(claimed_error, 1e-6))),
    empirical_Q = pmin(60, -10 * log10(ifelse(n_wrong == 0, zero_error_upper, observed_error))), # zero errors plotted at the lower bound
    bar_Q_low = pmin(60, -10 * log10(ifelse(n_wrong == 0, zero_error_upper, boot_error_high))),
    bar_Q_high = ifelse(n_wrong == 0, 60, pmin(60, -10 * log10(pmax(boot_error_low, 1e-6)))),
    point_type = ifelse(n_wrong == 0, "No errors (lower bound)", "Errors observed"),
    group = factor(group, levels = calibration_groups))

### Step 7: GQ threshold trade-off
# GQ as a filter: share of calls kept and share of wrong calls thrown out, per depth and threshold
gq_tradeoff_table <- bind_rows(lapply(gq_thresholds_to_test, function(threshold) {
  downsampled_calls_scored %>%
    summarise(gq_threshold = threshold,
              share_kept = mean(GQ_stan >= threshold),
              share_errors_removed = sum(stan_wrong & GQ_stan < threshold) / sum(stan_wrong), # NaN = no errors at this depth
              error_among_kept = sum(stan_wrong & GQ_stan >= threshold) / sum(GQ_stan >= threshold), # NaN = no call passes
              .by = depth)
}))

kable(gq_tradeoff_table %>% filter(gq_threshold %in% c(0, 10, 20, 30)) %>%
        mutate(share_kept = round(100 * share_kept, 1), error_among_kept = round(100 * error_among_kept, 3)) %>%
        arrange(depth, gq_threshold)) 

### Step 8: Saving tables and everything else the plot chunk needs

write_tsv(error_by_depth_table, file.path(downsampling_output_folder, "error_vs_depth.tsv"))
write_tsv(calibration_table, file.path(downsampling_output_folder, "genotype_calibration.tsv"))
write_tsv(calibration_statistics_table, file.path(downsampling_output_folder, "calibration_statistics.tsv"))
write_tsv(gq_tradeoff_table, file.path(downsampling_output_folder, "gq_cutoff_tradeoff.tsv"))
write_tsv(downsampled_calls_scored %>% select(pair_id, true_class, called_class, depth, k, prior_hom1, prior_hom2, prior_het, genotype_naive,
genotype_stan, max_posterior_stan, GQ_stan, naive_wrong, stan_wrong),
          file.path(downsampling_output_folder, "downsampled_calls.tsv"))

# Prior written out for the plot subtitles
prior_description <- switch(prior_type,
  flat = "flat",
  het_share = sprintf("het share %s", prior_het_share),
  hwe = prior_population,
  ancestry = sprintf("learned ancestry, %s vs FreqDOG", prior_population))

# Creates one .rds file with everything the plotting chunk needs
downsampling_plot_inputs <- list(
  error_by_depth_table = error_by_depth_table,
  calibration_table = calibration_table,
  calibration_statistics_table = calibration_statistics_table,
  gq_tradeoff_table = gq_tradeoff_table,
  n_truth_pairs = nrow(truth_pairs),
  draws_per_depth = draws_per_depth,
  bootstrap_rounds = bootstrap_rounds,
  calibration_groups = calibration_groups,
  prior_description = prior_description)

saveRDS(downsampling_plot_inputs, file.path(downsampling_output_folder, "downsampling_plot_inputs.rds"))
```
